challenge.better_approach: Considered reading the index's git history (git log -p) for the first entry. It is exact across boxes but costs a git walk per sweep over a 10 MB file. The trail costs nothing and the sweep only reports.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That this box's doors wrote the ticket. A ticket cast on another box has no trail entry here and reads past_horizon. That is honest, but it is not 'pre_door'.
challenge.prior_art: b15da5656579 adds read_trail for exactly these readers. Grepped tickets/ for sweep_casts: only 23089d52d805, which built it.
challenge.real_collision: None. 23089d52d805's classes stay; past_horizon is added beside them.

answers.falsifier: Done when the sweep classifies a twice-written ticket by its first entry and a ticket past the horizon reads past_horizon. Wrong if a reader needs the first entry of a ticket older than 30 days; then it must read git history.
answers.how: Swap door.read_journal(commons_root) for door.read_trail(commons_root) in sweep_casts and in the probe. A ticket whose first entry is past the trail's horizon gets its own class, past_horizon, rather than reading as unjournaled. The docstrings and the probe's finding name the 30-day horizon. A red-first proof writes a ticket twice through a scratch world's door and checks that the sweep classifies it by its first entry.
answers.traces_to: Law 3: a census that reads one entry per ticket reports a class it never measured. Law 7: an old ticket read as unjournaled is a false red in a record of truth.
answers.what: cast.py sweep_casts and the the_casting_door_has_callers probe read every entry from artifact.read_trail instead of the newest-per-path index, and say that the census covers 30 days.

bullets.text: the cast census becomes a 30-day, per-box census
